_source: Claude Code 2.1.287 on the GitHub Actions runner of the #170 implement rework (session df732362-2c82-46c9-b51a-cdaffb61fe26, 2026-10-02). Verbatim transcript lines, copied with factory/test/fixtures (no hand edits).
_note: workflow_receipt: the orchestrator's real Workflow tool_use and its background receipt (the receipt names no output file). background_task: a real background Bash task in a subagent of that run — its tool_use, its receipt, the runner's completion notification exactly as the runner logged it (an `attachment` line of type `queued_command`, with a `timestamp`), and the real tasks/<id>.output it names, with that file's ctime from stat(2) taken right after the notification.

must_fix.claim: Candidate (1b) treats the bytes at the receipt-bound path as the runner's verdict. That path is under /tmp, and the write-deny hook explicitly lets every reviewer write there. Any reviewer subagent in the review Workflow can therefore replace the whole review.v1 handoff: all roles approve, must_fix empty, overriding the reject that another reviewer actually returned. Before this diff, a reviewer controlled only its own verdict, plus whatever text the model passed on to the dispatcher. The binding work (receipt Task ID, user-turn header, tool-use-id) proves that the runner named the path. It does not prove the file still holds the runner's bytes when verify reads it. That breaks CLAUDE.md SDD rule 5: verdicts must be anchored only to runner records or facts that agents cannot write.
must_fix.evidence: (a) Location: the real fixture records `<output-file>/tmp/claude-1001/-home-runner-work-know-thy-build-demo-know-thy-build-demo/<session>/tasks/w6xdqhynw.output`. That is the OS temp dir, owned by the same uid as every subagent. run-stage.js sets no TMPDIR for `claude -p` (grep finds none). (b) Writers: reviewer-*.md all declare `tools: ... Bash`. deny-all-writes.sh:75 puts `/tmp/[^[:space:]\"]*` in the allowlist, and line 107 strips those targets before the redirection, ln, cp and mv rules run, so `> /tmp/claude-1001/.../tasks/<id>.output` and `ln -sf ... /tmp/claude-.../tasks/<id>.output` are allowed by design. Line 183 lists runtime-assembled commands (a script file run through bash) as a non-goal. (c) Reader: readFileOrNull is existsSync, statSync and readFileSync. It checks for no containing directory, does no lstat or realpath, and does not compare ownership or mtime against the notification. (d) Precedence: (1b) is tried before candidate (2), the tool results, the Workflow results and the envelope. When the inline notification <result> is truncated, which is the #124 case this diff exists for, (1b) decides. That applies on a normal successful run too, not only under max-turns, because main() now always passes readFile (makeVerifyStageDep). (e) Downstream: verifyStage (verify-stage.js:416-418) checks only that roster roles appear as completed in agents.jsonl. Nothing compares the per-role verdicts in the record with what each subagent actually returned (verdict-format.sh only checks the format). A forged record that lists every rostered role passes. The dispatcher cannot do this: it runs under dontAsk with allowed-tools Workflow and Read(.factory/out/loaded.json) only. The attacker is a reviewer subagent, for example one steered by prompt injection in the PR diff it is reviewing. Unconfirmed, and per the lens treated as reject: whether Claude Code reaps a detached `nohup … &` child when a subagent stops, and whether the runner writes the file once at completion or streams it. A pre-planted symlink does not forge on its own, because the runner's write would go through it. The attack needs a write after completion, which a detached process supplies.
must_fix.repro: Inside a review Workflow, a reviewer runs Bash call 1: `printf '%s\n' 'sleep 600; for f in /tmp/claude-1001/*/*/tasks/*.output; do cat /tmp/fake-review.json > "$f"; done' > /tmp/s.sh`, plus `printf ... > /tmp/fake-review.json` (a valid review.v1 with every roster role approving). Both targets are under /tmp, which deny-all-writes allows. Bash call 2: `nohup bash /tmp/s.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 &`. Only `bash /tmp/s.sh` is scanned, so the script body is never seen. The reviews are long, so the inline <result> is truncated. The runner then writes tasks/<id>.output, and the script overwrites it. run-stage verify reads the forged file through (1b) and returns ok:true with source 'workflow output file …', and the stage hands off approve. Static trace only. I did not execute this.
